title: Career Roadmap: Consultant
summary: A Consultant helps organizations understand problems, evaluate evidence, develop strategies and improve decisions. Graduates of integrated M.A. programmes in Economics, English or Development Studies can enter consulting by combining their subject expertise with research, analytical thinking, communication and project-management skills.

facts.Current degree: Integrated / Dual-Degree Programmes (BS-MS, B.Tech+M.Tech, B.Sc-M.Sc, BA-MA)

blocks.text: A Consultant helps organizations understand problems, evaluate evidence, develop strategies and improve decisions. Graduates of integrated M.A. programmes in Economics, English or Development Studies can enter consulting by combining their subject expertise with research, analytical thinking, communication and project-management skills.
The exact career path depends on the specialization:

blocks.label: Economics
blocks.text: Economic research, business analysis, market intelligence and policy consulting.

blocks.label: English
blocks.text: Communications consulting, content strategy, editorial services and knowledge management.

blocks.label: Development Studies
blocks.text: Social-impact consulting, public policy, programme evaluation and development-sector advisory.
Core responsibility
Investigate a client's problem, collect and interpret information, recommend practical solutions and communicate findings clearly.
Work environments
Consulting firms, research organizations, NGOs, government advisory projects, corporate strategy teams and independent consultancies.

rows.text: Integrated M.A. in Economics, English or Development Studies
Often 5 years; confirm the programme structure of the institution
Research methods, subject specialization, critical analysis, writing and presentation
Excel, data interpretation, report writing, presentation tools and project planning
Research internships, consulting projects, case studies and client-facing assignments
Optional MBA, public policy, applied economics, development management or a relevant specialist qualification

blocks.text: An integrated M.A. provides subject knowledge, but consulting is a broad occupation. Students should select a consulting specialization and build the practical skills that employers in that field expect.
Years 1–2
Build analytical foundations

items.text: Develop critical thinking, research, reading and professional writing.
Learn to identify problems, evaluate sources and summarize evidence.
Strengthen Excel, presentations and basic quantitative reasoning.
Explore economics, communications or development-sector consulting.

blocks.text: Years 3–4
Develop consulting skills

items.text: Choose a specialization and study relevant industry problems.
Learn data analysis, stakeholder interviews and report preparation.
Practise case studies, presentations and evidence-based recommendations.
Participate in research projects, internships or consulting competitions.

blocks.text: Year 5
Prepare for employment

items.text: Complete a dissertation, applied research project or internship.
Build a portfolio with research reports, case studies and recommendations.
Practise consulting interviews and structured problem-solving.
Apply for analyst, research associate, consulting associate and programme analyst roles.

blocks.text: Economics and Business Consulting
Suitable for Economics graduates interested in market research, economic analysis, pricing, public finance and business strategy.

blocks.label: Potential roles
blocks.text: Economic Analyst, Market Research Analyst, Business Consulting Analyst.
Communications and Content Consulting
Suitable for English graduates interested in corporate communication, content strategy, editorial consulting and knowledge management.

blocks.label: Potential roles
blocks.text: Communications Analyst, Content Strategist, Editorial Consultant.
Development and Public Policy Consulting
Suitable for Development Studies graduates interested in social-impact programmes, public policy, livelihoods, education and programme evaluation.

blocks.label: Potential roles
blocks.text: Development Analyst, Policy Research Associate, Monitoring and Evaluation Associate.

Useful tools include Excel, PowerPoint, Google Workspace, survey platforms and data-visualization tools. Economics-focused roles may benefit from SQL, Python or R, while communications roles may require content-management and editorial tools.
Explore internships with:

items.text: Management and specialist consulting firms.
Economic research and market intelligence organizations.
Public policy think tanks.
NGOs and social-impact organizations.
Corporate communications and content agencies.
Research institutes and programme evaluation teams.

blocks.text: Recommended portfolio projects

blocks.label: Business consulting
blocks.text: Analyse a hypothetical business problem and recommend measurable improvements.

blocks.label: Economic research
blocks.text: Study a public economic dataset and prepare a short evidence-based report.

blocks.label: Communications strategy
blocks.text: Create a communication plan for a defined audience and organizational objective.

blocks.label: Development consulting
blocks.text: Evaluate a public programme using clearly defined indicators and available evidence.

blocks.label: Policy brief
blocks.text: Write a concise brief explaining a policy problem, available evidence, alternative solutions and trade-offs.
Clearly label simulated projects as academic exercises. For real consulting assignments, obtain permission to share client information and respect confidentiality.
Potential areas for supplementary learning include:

items.text: Excel and business data analysis.
Consulting case interviews and structured problem-solving.
Project management fundamentals.
Research methodology and survey design.
Monitoring and evaluation for development projects.
Business communication and presentation skills.
Public policy analysis or applied economics, depending on specialization.

blocks.text: Certifications can demonstrate initiative, but employers will also evaluate analytical ability, communication, work samples and relevant experience. An MBA or another postgraduate qualification may help with particular consulting career paths, but it is not universally required for entry-level consulting work.
Research Intern / Analyst Intern
Research, data gathering and documentation
Junior Consultant / Consulting Analyst
Analysis, presentations and project support
Consultant / Senior Consultant
Own workstreams and advise clients or stakeholders
Project Manager / Principal Consultant
Lead projects, client relationships and specialist teams

Career progression varies by consulting field and employer. Some specialists progress toward research leadership, policy advisory, communications leadership or independent consulting rather than general management consulting.

items.text: AI-assisted research and evidence synthesis.
Economic forecasting and data-informed strategy.
Digital communications and content strategy.
ESG and sustainability advisory.
Public policy and social-impact evaluation.
Monitoring, evaluation and learning for development programmes.
Responsible AI, governance and organizational change.

blocks.text: AI tools can help summarize information and organize research, but consultants must verify sources, protect confidential information and independently evaluate recommendations.
Preparation progress
Choose a consulting specialization aligned with the M.A. subject
Build research, writing and presentation skills
Learn Excel and relevant data-analysis tools
Complete at least two practical case studies or research projects
Complete a relevant internship or supervised project
Prepare a résumé and portfolio of analytical work
Practise structured problem-solving and interview questions

blocks.label: Final recommendation
blocks.text: Students pursuing an integrated M.A. should build consulting expertise around their academic subject instead of treating consulting as a single, uniform career. Economics students can prioritize quantitative and market analysis, English students can focus on communications and content strategy, and Development Studies students can emphasize policy research and programme evaluation. Practical projects, internships and clear evidence-based recommendations are the foundation for entry-level opportunities.
